title: Identify Inputs, Outputs, State, and Side Effects
learningObjectives: Define inputs, outputs, state, and side effects.
Classify these elements in a realistic program.
Trace how inputs affect state and outputs.
Distinguish returned values from observable side effects.
Explain how separating data roles supports testing.

understand.concept: Inputs are received information; outputs are results; state is information maintained or changed; side effects are observable changes such as printing, file writes, database updates, network requests, or shared-data mutation. Define the system boundary to classify them accurately.
understand.whyItMatters: Mapping these roles makes data flow clearer and helps detect hidden dependencies and unintended changes.
understand.analogy: A vending machine accepts selections and payment, maintains stock and credit, dispenses an item, and updates inventory.
understand.analogyLimit: Roles depend on the boundary: something may be an input to one component and an output from another.

explain.narrative: Draw the system boundary, list inputs and outputs, identify state variables and changes, and record side effects. Trace data through the system. Keep calculations pure where practical and isolate side effects.

examples.title: Inputs and output
examples.explanation: Width and height are inputs; area is the output.

examples.title: Changing state
examples.explanation: Score is maintained state and changes over time.

examples.title: Mutation side effect
examples.explanation: The array is changed by adding an element.

examples.title: Pure calculation
examples.explanation: It returns a value without changing external state.

examples.title: Separate data roles
examples.explanation: Distinct names clarify the flow from input to calculated output.

commonMistakes: Calling changing state a fixed input.
Ignoring database, file, or network changes.
Confusing returned values with printed output.
